Another analyst suggests Thailand is portraying the clashes as a necessary response to Cambodian aggression to divert attention from its own internal instability.

titleEn: BREAKING: Senior Chinese Foreign Ministry official to visit Cambodia and Thailand to restore peace quickly

summary: The Thai-Cambodia People Alliance for Peace has called for an immediate ceasefire, accusing both governments of using the border dispute to fuel 'ultranationalism' and distract from internal political failures. The article also mentions a Thai airstrike that damaged a primary school in Thmar Pouk district on December 17.

He specifically cited reports of Thai bombs falling near refugee camps.

She listed the weapons used as DK guns, 100mm tank guns, 105mm and 155mm artillery, toxic gas drones, fire drones, and suicide drones. Attacks targeted Prasat Ta Moan Thom and areas near Preah Vihear Temple. Cambodia called on the international community to condemn these actions as 'illegal war crimes.'

Cambodian forces remain on high alert and have reportedly fired back to defend territorial integrity.

Almost 500,000 people have been displaced.

The report also alleges that Thai forces used toxic gas drones at 10:29 AM in the Preah Vihear temple area. Cambodian forces remain on high alert to protect territorial integrity.

titleEn: Ministry of Defense: Day 12, Thai military continues shooting and invading Cambodian sovereignty, using F-16s to drop bombs on civilian sites and firing toxic gas

summary: Reports indicate sustained aerial bombardment by Thai F-16 aircraft in the Banteay Meanchey sector. Cambodian forces remain on high alert and are reportedly firing back to protect territorial integrity.

summary: Tens of thousands of Cambodians, led by Hun Many of the Union of Youth Federations of Cambodia (UYFC), gathered in Phnom Penh to call for an end to the conflict and a return to the Kuala Lumpur ceasefire agreement. Participants urged both sides to stop the violence that has killed at least 55 people and displaced hundreds of thousands.
title: Thousands of Cambodians hold peace rally, urge respect for ceasefire amid border clashes with Thailand

The Cambodian side maintains it has no intention of taking what is not theirs but will not accept any loss of territory.

It frames the actions as a 'deliberate escalation' and an 'offensive act of war' that violates the UN Charter. titleEn: Interior Ministry: 18 Cambodian civilians killed and 79 injured due to Thai soldiers invading Cambodia

The statement demands that Thailand take responsibility for 'war crimes' and violations of international law following 12 days of aggression.

titleEn: Cambodian Defense Ministry calls on Thai army to immediately stop lying and return to the path of peace

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense released a detailed timeline for December 18, 2025, marking the 12th day of conflict. In the afternoon, multiple bombings were reported in Serei Saophoan city. The ministry also accused Thai forces of using 'poisonous smoke' (gas) in the Preah Vihear and 5 January mountain areas.

Official reports indicate the conflict has claimed at least 55 lives so far, including 18 Cambodian civilians and 16 Thai civilians, along with numerous military casualties on both sides.

Significant damage was reported to civilian infrastructure including schools, health centers, and pagodas. The government called for international intervention to compel Thailand to return to the ceasefire agreement.

They urged both governments to respect previous peace agreements and restore normalcy for people living along the border.

In Military Zone 5 (Banteay Meanchey/Pursat), reports include Thai drone strikes in Thma Da and artillery fire from a warship in the same area. The ministry claims Thai forces fired shells into civilian homes in Banteay Mean Rith.

He described the loss as 'regrettable but unavoidable' during military operations. He acknowledged Cambodia's air defense capabilities and stated that security has been tightened across all armed forces units following the incident and the discovery of drones near oil rigs in the Gulf of Thailand.

titleEn: Thai Defense Minister admits Cambodia really has the capability to shoot down its drones

titleEn: Ministry of National Defense: At 15:30, the Thai military used F-16 fighter jets to drop bombs in Peak Sbeak, Preah Vihear province

summary: China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi held telephone calls with his Cambodian and Thai counterparts, Prak Sokhonn and Sihasak Phuangketkeow, on Thursday. China is acting as a mediator, urging both sides to reach a ceasefire before the situation undermines ASEAN unity. Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense also issued a statement condemning Thailand for using F-16s and heavy artillery against schools and civilian areas, insisting that Cambodian military moves are purely defensive. ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn warned that the bloc cannot ignore the fighting which has displaced over 500,000 people.
title: Beijing Steps In to Mediate as Cambodia, Thailand Seek to Defuse Border Conflict

titleEn: Conflict Update 16:00 19/12/25: Thai F16s strike Cambodia again

summary: Internal political observers are urging the ruling Hun family to arrest high-level 'criminal masterminds' within Cambodia. This is seen as a move to strip Thailand of its international diplomatic justification for the border conflict, which Thailand claims is partly about addressing cross-border crime and scam hubs. The article highlights that unless the Cambodian government takes action against these figures, Thailand will continue to use the narrative of law enforcement to justify its military presence and 'invasion' of Khmer territory.

titleEn: Observers tell Hun family to arrest criminal masterminds so Thailand cannot use this story to mislead international community

summary: Cambodian analysts and legal experts rejected Thailand's claims that its military operations were intended to suppress online scam gangs. Lawyer Sok Sam Oeun stated that bombing ancient temples and bridges with F-16s has nothing to do with fighting criminals and is instead an attempt to destroy Cambodia's military capacity. Experts accused Thailand of using these narratives to distract from violations of international law and to cover up internal issues.

titleEn: Thailand is trying to divert the situation to avoid responsibility for the war of aggression against Cambodia

summary: The Thai government, through its Joint Information Center for the Thai-Cambodian Situation, has expressed hope for a ceasefire before December 25. However, Bangkok insists that Cambodia must first accept three unilateral conditions: 1) Cambodia must declare a ceasefire first, 2) The ceasefire must be subject to physical and continuous investigation, and 3) Cambodia must cooperate in joint demining operations. Cambodian analysts have called these conditions 'unacceptable,' arguing that Thailand is the aggressor and should be the one to implement such measures. This development comes as ASEAN Foreign Ministers prepare to meet on December 22 to discuss the conflict.
title: ថៃ ចង់មានបទឈប់បាញ់នៅមុនបុណ្យណូអែល ប៉ុន្ដែនៅតែទទូចឱ្យកម្ពុជា ទទួលយកលក្ខខណ្ឌ 3ចំណុច ដែលខ្លួនបានកំណត់
titleEn: Thailand wants a ceasefire before Christmas but still insists Cambodia accepts 3 conditions it has set

summary: On the morning of December 20, a large Thai military drone reportedly violated Cambodian sovereignty by flying deep into Veal Veng District, Pursat Province, reaching the 1500 Mountain area. The report characterizes this as a serious territorial violation.

He also called for the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers currently detained by Thailand.
title: ASEAN backs peaceful solution, urges ceasefire in Cambodia-Thailand dispute, Cambodian top diplomat says

summary: The Ministry of National Defence reported that Thai F-16 fighter jets dropped 6 bombs on the Koul 8 area and Satsat village in Preah Vihear province between 14:30 and 15:10. Additional bombs were dropped in Banteay Ampil district. Shelling also continued near Ta Moan and Chub Kakir temples, and 10 shells hit civilian locations in Poipet.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 16.20 23/12/25: Thai F-16s stage multiple bombing raids on Cambodia

summary: The Cambodian Red Cross (CRC) has dispatched 100 tonnes of rice, drinking water, and other supplies to Banteay Meanchey, Oddar Meanchey, Preah Vihear, Battambang, and Pursat provinces. These supplies are intended for hundreds of thousands of civilians displaced by the ongoing border conflict. The move follows reports of over 500,000 Cambodians currently seeking shelter in internal displacement camps.
title: CRC sends rice, drinking water to displaced at border

summary: The Cambodian Mine Action Authority (CMAA) has officially rejected allegations from the Thai military that Cambodia is laying new landmines along the border. The CMAA stated that these accusations are based on unilateral claims by the Thai side without evidence. Cambodia maintains that any mine incidents are from older, pre-existing mines from past conflicts.
title: យោធាថៃ ចោទកម្ពុជាដាក់មីនថ្មី គឺពឹងផ្អែកលើការអះអាងជាឯកតោភាគី
titleEn: Thai military's accusation of Cambodia laying new mines is a unilateral claim

summary: A planned General Border Committee (GBC) meeting to negotiate an end to border clashes is in doubt as both sides disagree on a venue. Cambodia requested to hold the talks in a neutral third country (Kuala Lumpur), citing security concerns, while Thailand insists the bilateral meeting should proceed in Thailand's Chanthaburi province. Over 80 people have reportedly died since fighting resumed in early December.
title: Thailand-Cambodia border meeting in doubt over venue row

summary: On December 23, the Thai military reportedly intensified its assault by firing over 300 artillery shells into Cambodian territory, specifically targeting areas in Banteay Meanchey, Oddar Meanchey, Battambang, and Pursat provinces. Specific incidents included shelling in Sampov Loun district and moving tanks and armored vehicles into the Chai Chumneah border pass area.
title: យោធាថៃសន្ធប់បាញ់គ្រាប់ផ្លោងចូលកម្ពុជា ជាង300គ្រាប់ នៅថ្ងៃ23 ធ្នូនេះ
titleEn: Thai military fired more than 300 shells into Cambodia on December 23

summary: Military and defense officials from Cambodia and Thailand are scheduled to meet on December 24, 2025, for a General Border Committee (GBC) meeting. The talks will focus on ceasefire implementation and verification. The EU has reportedly offered satellite imagery to assist in monitoring the ceasefire. The meeting is expected to take place in Chanthaburi, Thailand.
title: កម្ពុជា-ថៃ នឹងបើកកិច្ចប្រជុំ GBC នៅថ្ងៃស្អែក
titleEn: Cambodia-Thailand to hold GBC meeting tomorrow

summary: Officials from the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training released a formal petition on December 24 strongly condemning the 'inhumane' actions of the Thai military. The petition accuses Thailand of repeatedly violating ceasefire agreements signed under international witnesses and calls on the international community to hold Thailand accountable for civilian casualties and displacement.
title: ក្រសួងការងារចេញញត្តិថ្កោលទោសសង្គ្រាមឈ្លានពានរបស់ថៃ មកលើអធិបតេយ្យភាពនៃព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Ministry of Labour issues petition condemning Thailand's war of aggression against Cambodia's sovereignty

summary: As of 7:30 AM on Wednesday, Thai forces continued to shell several sectors including Prey Chan, Preah Vihear Temple, and Mount Kham. Shelling was specifically reported around 5:00 AM at Ta Moan and Chubkakir temples. While Pursat province remained quiet, active fire was maintained in the northern and northwestern military regions.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 08.00 24/12/25: Sporadic shelling on Cambodian border
titleEn: Conflict Update 08:00 24/12/25: Sporadic shelling on Cambodian border

summary: New reports indicate Thai F-16 fighter jets conducted a raid approximately 60km inside Cambodian territory near Phnom Sampov in Battambang. The Ministry of Defence confirmed that 6 bombs were dropped during this mission at around 10:00 AM on Wednesday.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 10:40 24/12/25: Thai F-16s attack Cambodia again in raid 60km into The Kingdom

summary: Fighting continued on the morning of December 24 as the General Border Committee (GBC) secretariat prepared to meet. The Defense Ministry reported that Thai T-50 aircraft dropped four bombs in Banan district, leading to the closure of 241 schools. Military spokesperson Maly Socheata claimed Thai forces used toxic gas drones near Preah Vihear. Displaced Cambodian civilians now exceed 600,000.
title: Cambodia-Thailand Border Clash Continues Ahead of GBC Meeting, Cambodian Defense Ministry States

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that at 10:00 AM on December 24, Thai forces used South Korean-made T-50 fighter jets to drop bombs in the Phnom Sampov area of Banan district, approximately 100km from the border. The ministry condemned the act as a 'brutal war crime' and indiscriminate attack on civilians.
title: ថៃយកយន្តហោះចម្បាំង T-50 របស់កូរ៉េខាងត្បូង ទម្លាក់គ្រាប់បែក4គ្រាប់ក្បែរសាលារៀនក្នុងខេត្តបាត់ដំបង
titleEn: Thailand uses South Korean T-50 fighter jets to drop 4 bombs near school in Battambang

summary: Defense Ministry spokesperson Mali Socheata confirmed that as of Wednesday, the 18th day of conflict, 21 Cambodian civilians have died and 83 are injured. Shelling continued this morning in Poipet (near Roundabout 58) and O'Chrov district, injuring two more civilians just hours before the GBC meeting in Chanthaburi.
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិកម្ពុជាអះអាងថា ការប៉ះទង្គិចគ្នាតាមព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ នៅតែបន្តមុនកិច្ចប្រជុំគណៈកម្មាធិការព្រំដែនទូទៅ
titleEn: Cambodia-Thailand border clash continues ahead of GBC meeting, Cambodian Defense Ministry states

summary: The Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Lin Jian, called for an immediate ceasefire and dialogue. Separately, the Cambodian Ministry of Defense accused Thailand of dropping 'cluster bombs' in Svay Chek district, Banteay Meanchey, between 12:15 PM and 12:26 PM today, further complicating peace efforts.
title: ក្រសួងការបរទេសចិន ឆ្លើយតបចំពោះជម្លោះកម្ពុជាថៃ ៖ ប្រទេសចិន នឹងបន្តជំរុញយ៉ាងសកម្ម ឱ្យមានការចរចាសន្តិភាព
titleEn: Chinese Foreign Ministry responds to Cambodia-Thai conflict: China will continue to actively promote peace talks

summary: Local reports from the border area of Ou Skach confirm that a female elephant and its newly born calf were killed by shrapnel from Thai artillery shelling. The report frames this as part of the broader destruction caused by 'Thai invaders' against Cambodian natural resources and wildlife.
title: រកឃើញដំរីញី 1ក្បាល និងកូនទើបកើត 1ក្បាល ស្លាប់ដោយសារអំបែងគ្រាប់ផ្ទុះ របស់ទាហានឈ្លានពានថៃ នៅចំណុចអូរស្កាច
titleEn: Mother elephant and newborn calf found dead due to shrapnel from Thai invaders at Ou Skach

summary: A detailed situational report indicates that between 6:00 PM on Dec 23 and early morning on Dec 24, Thai artillery targeted Koul 8, Phnom Trangol, Ta Sim, and Preah Vihear temple. At midnight, long-distance shelling was reported specifically hitting the Preah Vihear temple area. The report characterizes these as indiscriminate attacks in violation of international law.
title: Conflict Update: Situation Update on Escalating Thai Military Attacks and Violations of Cambodian Sovereignty Along the Cambodia–Thailand Border (4th and 5th Military Regions)

summary: Authorities in Banan district, Battambang, have ordered the immediate closure of 83 schools, including 3 high schools and 10 secondary schools, after Thai T-50 fighter jets reportedly dropped 4 bombs in civilian areas of Chhoeu Teal commune. The district governor, Sreng Sokha, stated the move is to ensure the safety of over 20,000 students as residents flee the area in fear.
title: អាជ្ញាធរស្រុកបាណន់សម្រេចបិទសាលា83ខ្នងភ្លាមៗ ក្រោយយន្តហោះចម្បាំងថៃទម្លាក់គ្រាប់ចូលភូមិសាស្រ្តស្រុកបាណន់
titleEn: Banan district authorities decides to close 83 schools immediately after Thai soldiers use aircraft drop bombs into Banan area

summary: Thailand has proposed three conditions for the GBC talks starting at 4:00 PM today in Chanthaburi. The conditions include: Cambodia must announce a genuine ceasefire, the ceasefire must be monitored by observers, and Cambodia must cooperate on landmine clearance. The ministerial meeting on Dec 27 depends on the success of these Secretariat-level talks.
title: Thailand sets conditions ahead of Cambodia–Thailand GBC talks in Chanthaburi

summary: Thai forces intensified aerial attacks on December 24 by deploying KAI T-50TH Golden Eagle jet fighters alongside F-16s. Between 12:15 PM and 2:02 PM, these aircraft reportedly dropped cluster bombs in Svay Chek district (Banteay Meanchey) and Banan district (Battambang). The report describes villagers, including women who recently gave birth, fleeing to rice fields in fear.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 15:00 24/12/25: Thailand adds T-50TH jet fighters to intensify aerial bombing of Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 15:00 24/12/25: Thailand adds T-50TH jet fighters to intensify aerial bombing of Cambodia

summary: Russian Ambassador Anatoly Borovik presented 2 tonnes of rice, cooking oil, noodles, and water to the Cambodian Red Cross (CRC) to support families displaced by the border conflict. The donation was received by CRC Secretary-General Pum Chantinie at their headquarters. Ambassador Borovik expressed condolences for the loss of life and reaffirmed Moscow's humanitarian commitment to Cambodia.
title: Russian Embassy donates supplies to CRC for displaced

summary: Military delegates from both nations met at the Ban Phak Kat checkpoint in Thailand's Chanthaburi province on Wednesday afternoon. Led by Major General Nhem Boraden (Cambodia) and General Nuttapong Praokaew (Thailand), the secretariat meeting aims to set the agenda for formal ministerial talks on December 27. The discussions are focused on establishing a ceasefire and monitoring mechanisms under the watch of ASEAN Observer Teams (AOT).
title: Thailand and Cambodia start the General Border Committee secretariat meeting

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Defense reported that Thai fighter jets dropped cluster bombs in Banteay Meanchey and four bombs into civilian areas in Battambang on Wednesday. Thai Army spokesperson Winthai Suvaree countered that any munitions used were directed strictly at military targets and are not meant to harm civilians. He also noted that neither nation is bound by the Convention on Cluster Munitions as they are not signatories.
title: Cambodia says Thailand drops cluster bombs, Thailand claims only targets military objectives

summary: A wild elephant and her newborn calf were found dead in a pond inside the Preah Rokar-Chep Wildlife Sanctuary in Preah Vihear province on December 22. Environmental authorities and park rangers confirmed the deaths were caused by shrapnel from Thai military shelling. Environment Minister Eang Sophalleth condemned the incident, stating that the conflict is destroying Cambodia's natural resources and biodiversity in addition to human lives.
title: Shrapnel from shelling kills wild elephant, calf in Preah Vihear sanctuary

summary: According to the Ministry of National Defense, a Cambodian civilian was killed on the morning of December 25 when Thai forces fired 155mm heavy artillery into Talei village, Thma Puok district, Banteay Meanchey province. This latest casualty brings the total number of Cambodian civilians killed in the border conflict to 30 people.
title: ជម្លោះព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ បណ្ដាលឱ្យពលរដ្ឋស្លូតត្រង់កម្ពុជាបាត់បង់ជីវិត 30 នាក់ហើយ
titleEn: Cambodia-Thailand border conflict has killed 30 innocent Cambodian civilians

summary: One Cambodian civilian was killed at 8:41 a.m. on December 25, 2025, due to Thai military shelling in Taley village, Kouk Romiet commune, Thma Puok district, Banteay Meanchey province. The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense condemned the attack as a violation of international humanitarian law.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 09.30 25/12/25: Cambodian civilian killed by renewed Thai shelling
titleEn: Conflict Update 09:30 Dec 25, 2025: Cambodian civilian killed by renewed Thai shelling

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that at 8:41 a.m. on December 25, Thai military forces fired 155mm artillery shells into a civilian residential area in Ta Lei village, Kouk Romiet commune, Thmar Pouk district, Banteay Meanchey province. The attack resulted in the death of one innocent Cambodian civilian. The ministry described the actions as 'indiscriminate' and a violation of international humanitarian law.
title: Defence Ministry: Thai Military Fires 155mm Artillery into Cambodian Civilian Area, One Killed

summary: The second day of the General Border Committee (GBC) Secretariat Meeting began at 9:05 a.m. at the Prom-Pak Kard border crossing between Pailin and Chanthaburi. Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata stated that technical teams are discussing mechanisms for a cessation of hostilities. This meeting serves as preparation for the 3rd Special GBC Meeting scheduled for December 27, which will involve the Defense Ministers of both nations.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Start Second Day of GBC Secretariat Meeting

summary: Reports state that between 7:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. on December 25, Thai forces fired more than 30 artillery shells into Sampov Lun district, Battambang province. Additionally, 33 rounds of 155mm shells were reportedly fired into Talei village in Banteay Meanchey. The Cambodian side claims these areas are far from the disputed border zones, framing the shelling as a direct invasion of sovereignty.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 13.50 25/12/25: Thailand bombards Cambodian villages

summary: Defense Minister Tea Seiha sent best wishes to 18 soldiers (likely wounded or on the frontlines). Additionally, Information Minister Neth Pheaktra cited reports that Thai troops destroyed a Vishnu statue in a disputed area within Cambodian territory, an act condemned as a violation of cultural property and sovereignty.
title: នាយឧត្តមសេនីយ៍ ទៀ សីហា ជូនពរវីរកងទ័ពកម្ពុជា18រូប មានសុខភាពល្អ និងឆាប់វិលមកវិញ
titleEn: General Tea Seiha wishes 18 Cambodian hero soldiers good health and safe return

summary: Electricite du Cambodge (EDC) has joined other national institutions in issuing a formal petition condemning what they term as 'vicious and inhumane' acts by the Thai military. The petition supports the Royal Government of Cambodia's stance and calls for an immediate end to the shelling of innocent civilians along the border.
title: អគ្គិសនីកម្ពុជា ប្រកាសចេញញត្តិថ្កោលទោស សង្គ្រាមឈ្លានពានរបស់ថៃមកលើអធិបតេយ្យភាព នៃព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Electricite du Cambodge Issues Petition Condemning Thai Aggressive War Against Cambodia's Sovereignty

summary: On December 25, between 7:00 AM and 10:50 AM, the Thai military reportedly fired 33 heavy artillery shells into Taly village, Thmar Puok district, Banteay Meanchey. The strike killed one civilian and injured seven others. The Cambodian government condemned the attack as a 'cruel and inhumane' violation of international humanitarian law targeting civilian infrastructure.
title: យោធាថៃ បានបាញ់ផ្លោងកាំភ្លើងប្រភេទ 155ម.ម ចំនួន 33គ្រាប់ ចូលភូមិសាស្ត្រភូមិតាឡី ដើម្បី កម្ទេចលំនៅដ្ឋានរបស់ប្រជាពលរដ្ឋស៊ីវិលកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Thai military fired 33 shells of 155mm artillery into Taly village to destroy Cambodian civilian homes

summary: The Cambodian Senate issued a formal resolution condemning Thailand for what it calls a 'brutal and illegal invasion' from December 7 to 24. The statement cites the use of heavy artillery and fighter jets against civilians and historical temples, including Preah Vihear. The Senate claims these acts violate the UN Charter, the 1962 ICJ ruling, and recent ceasefire agreements from July and October 2025.
title: ព្រឹទ្ធសភា ប្រកាសចេញញត្តិថ្កោលទោស សង្គ្រាមឈ្លានពានរបស់ថៃ មកលើអធិបតេយ្យភាព នៃព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា
titleEn: Senate issues petition condemning Thai invasion of Cambodian sovereignty

summary: As of 2:30 p.m. on December 25, 2025, the Ministry of National Defense reported continued Thai shelling along the border in Banteay Meanchey (Svay Chek district), Oddar Meanchey, and Preah Vihear provinces (near Preah Vihear Temple and Veal Intri). In the Thamma Da area of Pursat, Thai drones reportedly dropped bombs on the Elephant River between 1:50 p.m. and 2:19 p.m.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 15.30 25/12/25: Thailand continues to shell Cambodia
titleEn: Conflict Update 15:30 Dec 25, 2025: Thailand continues to shell Cambodia

summary: Chinese Special Envoy Deng Xijun concluded a shuttle-diplomacy mission (Dec 18-23) to Cambodia and Thailand. He expressed condolences for the 30 Cambodian civilians reported killed as of the morning of Dec 25. China urged both sides to achieve an immediate ceasefire, restore trust, and support ASEAN mediation efforts.
title: China Expresses Hope for Restored Trust and Rebuilt Peace at Cambodia-Thailand Border

summary: A coalition of 896 Cambodian Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) submitted a petition to the international community condemning ongoing Thai military assaults. The petition highlights the use of cluster bombs and the destruction of cultural heritage, specifically the Ta Krabei Temple and damage to Preah Vihear Temple. The groups urge the UN and the international community to demand an immediate ceasefire and the withdrawal of Thai forces.
title: Cambodian Civil Society Organizations Submit Petition over Thai Military Intrusions into Cambodia's Sovereign Territory

summary: The Ministry of National Defense announced that between 10:00 AM and 12:00 PM on December 25, Thai forces fired 28 artillery shells into Sampov Loun district, Battambang province. Shelling also reportedly continued in Choke Chey village and Prey Chan village.
title: យោធាថៃ បាញ់ផ្លោងជិត30គ្រាប់ ចូលភូមិសាស្ត្រស្រុកសំពៅលូន
titleEn: Thai military shelled nearly 30 rounds into Sampov Loun district

summary: As the GBC Secretariat meeting entered its second day on December 25, Thai air attacks were reported in Battambang province. The article notes that national institutions and citizens are condemning the use of F-16 and T-50 warplanes. Additionally, a mother elephant and her calf were reportedly killed by Thai shelling in a sanctuary in Preah Vihear, sparking further outrage.
title: Cambodia - Thailand Border Talks Enter Second Day as Fighting Continues

summary: The Cambodian National Assembly issued a petition late December 24 condemning Thailand's 'brutal and inhumane invasion.' The statement claims Thailand has used heavy weapons including F-16 and T-50TH jets, warships, and cluster munitions, with strikes reaching 80–90 kilometers deep into Cambodia. It also accused Thailand of using 'toxic gas' and reported that 30 Cambodian civilians have been killed and over 630,000 displaced as of December 24.
title: Cambodia’s National Assembly Issues Petition Condemning Thailand’s Armed Invasion

summary: Reports indicate that Thai forces continued heavy shelling near the Preah Vihear Temple on the morning of December 25, despite UNESCO expressing deep concern over the risk to the World Heritage site. Portions of the temple are reportedly significantly damaged by the bombardment.
title: កងទ័ពថៃបន្តវាយសន្ធាប់មកលើតំបន់ប្រាសាទព្រះវិហារក្រោមក្រសែភ្នែកយូណេស្កូ
titleEn: Thai troops continue to attack Preah Vihear temple area under UNESCO watch

summary: Civil society groups from Cambodia and some Thai citizens are calling for an immediate end to hostilities as civilian casualties mount. The Ministry of Defense provided a detailed log for December 25, reporting heavy artillery (155mm) and DTI-2 rockets hitting Preah Vihear, Ta Moan, and O'Smach, alongside ground troop movements with tanks in Banteay Meanchey's Svay Chek commune.
title: អង្គការសង្គមស៊ីវិលកម្ពុជា និងពលរដ្ឋថៃទាមទារឱ្យបញ្ចប់ជម្លោះ ខណៈការស្លាប់របស់ជនស៊ីវិលកើនឡើង
titleEn: Cambodian CSOs and Thai citizens demand end to conflict as civilian deaths rise

summary: Nine more Cambodian civilians were reported killed yesterday, bringing the total death toll to 30. The article claims Thai air forces have struck targets as deep as 170 kilometers from the border despite ongoing General Border Committee (GBC) Secretariat talks in Pailin/Chanthaburi. Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn has briefed French officials on the deteriorating humanitarian situation involving over 640,000 displaced persons.
title: Civilian toll rises as Thai assaults continue despite ceasefire talks

summary: A ceasefire agreement is expected to be signed on December 27 following three days of intense negotiations at the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting at the Ban Phakkat/Prom border crossing. Despite ongoing reports of heavy shelling and airstrikes killing 31 civilians so far, Thai Prime Minister Anutin expressed optimism that the defense ministers of both nations will sign the document tomorrow. The agreement reportedly involves mine-clearing and the withdrawal of heavy weapons.
title: Cambodia–Thailand Ceasefire Set for December 27 After Border Talks

summary: As GBC Secretariat talks continue, Cambodia's Ministry of National Defence has officially rejected Thai media reports claiming Cambodia requested a ceasefire, labeling it a misinterpretation. On the night of December 25, PM Hun Manet spoke with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio via phone to discuss facilitating a rapid ceasefire and adhering to peace agreements.
title: Border talks underway as Phnom Penh rejects ceasefire claims

summary: On the night of December 25, 2025, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held a telephone conversation with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet. Rubio conveyed President Donald Trump's desire for peace and stated that the United States is ready to facilitate talks to end the weeks-long border clashes and restore stability. The call follows reports of nearly 100 deaths and hundreds of thousands of displaced civilians since fighting reignited on December 7.
title: លោក Rubio៖ អាមេរិកត្រៀមសម្របសម្រួលក្នុងកិច្ចចរចាសន្តិភាពរវាងកម្ពុជា និងថៃ
titleEn: Rubio: US ready to facilitate peace talks between Cambodia and Thailand

summary: The Cambodia-Thailand General Border Committee (GBC) Secretariat met for a third day in Chanthaburi to negotiate a path toward stability. Amidst these talks, at 9:46 AM on December 26, the Thai military reportedly fired two 155mm artillery shells into the Stung Bot area of Poipet, Banteay Meanchey. The article also mentions diplomatic mediation signals from Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim.
title: ក្រុមលេខាធិការ គណៈកម្មាធិការព្រំដែន ទូទៅកម្ពុជា-ថៃ (GBC) បន្ដកិច្ចប្រជុំថ្ងៃទី3 ដើម្បីឱ្យមាន ស្ថិរភាពឡើងវិញ រវាងប្រទេសទាំងពីរ
titleEn: GBC Secretariat continues Day 3 meeting to restore stability between both countries

summary: First Lady Pich Chanmony met with families displaced by the border conflict at Koh Pich in Phnom Penh. She expressed sympathy and provided aid to those affected by the ongoing military situation at the border.
title: លោកជំទាវបណ្ឌិត ពេជ ចន្ទមុន្នី ហ៊ុន ម៉ាណែត អញ្ជើញសំណេះសំណាលសួរសុខទុក្ខ និងផ្ដល់អំណោយជូនប្រជាជនភៀសសឹក ដោយសារការឈ្លានពានរបស់កងទ័ពថៃ នៅកោះពេជ្រ
titleEn: Dr. Pich Chanmony Hun Manet visits and provides gifts to people displaced by Thai military invasion at Koh Pich

summary: Officials from the Ministry of Information and the state news agency AKP delivered aid and school supplies to approximately 300 families displaced from Koh Kong province. These families fled to Srae Ambel district following Thai military aggression that began on December 13. While some families have started returning home, many remain in temporary shelters at local pagodas (such as Wat Sala Mnang) due to the unstable security situation.
title: មន្រ្តីក្រសួងព័ត៌មាននាំយកអំណោយចែកជូនជនភៀសសឹកនៅស្រុកស្រែអំបិល
titleEn: Information Ministry officials bring aid to displaced persons in Srae Ambel

summary: First Lady Dr. Pich Chanmony met with displaced families in border provinces on Friday to deliver humanitarian aid and encouragement. She conveyed support from Hun Sen, Bun Rany, and PM Hun Manet, emphasizing 'Khmer helping Khmer' while the government defends the nation and assists the hundreds of thousands forced to flee their homes.
title: Pich Chanmony provides support to civilians displaced by the Cambodia–Thailand border conflict

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense released a field report detailing Thai military actions on December 26. It reported that at 5:40 AM, Thai forces shelled Ta Krabey Temple, followed by artillery fire at Ta Moan Temple and Preah Vihear Temple. Most significantly, between 6:08 AM and 7:15 AM, Thai F-16 jets reportedly dropped 40 bombs on Chok Chey village, causing significant destruction. The ministry stated that Cambodian forces are fighting back with 'high vigilance.'
title: ក្រសួងការពារជាតិ ធ្វើបច្ចុប្បន្នភាពពីស្ថានពាក់ព័ន្ធករណីយោធាថៃ បន្តការបាញ់ប្រហារឈ្លានពានមកលើដែនអធិបតេយ្យកម្ពុជា រយៈពេល20ថ្ងៃ
titleEn: Ministry of National Defense updates on Thai military aggression over 20 days

summary: At approximately 1:00 PM on December 26, Thai fighter jets dropped 10 bombs in Srei Snam district, Siem Reap province. This area is located roughly 80km from the Thai border, marking a significant escalation and deep penetration into Cambodian territory. The report frames this as an attempt to invade Cambodian sovereignty beyond the disputed border zones.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 14.30 26/12/25: Thai F-16s bomb 80km inside Cambodian border

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation briefed representatives from 21 diplomatic missions on the latest border developments. Secretary of State Kung Phoak emphasized Cambodia's commitment to an immediate ceasefire and the peaceful resolution of disputes through existing bilateral mechanisms, while highlighting the impact of Thai military incursions on civilians.
title: Cambodia briefs foreign diplomats on developments in border tensions with Thailand

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet spoke by phone with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to discuss ways to secure a ceasefire. He emphasized Cambodia's commitment to the Kuala Lumpur Joint Statement and the July 28 truce framework to build long-term peace.
title: សម្តេចមហាបវរធិបតី ហ៊ុន ម៉ាណែត ជួបរដ្ឋមន្ត្រីការបរទេសអាមេរិក តាមទូរស័ព្ទ បញ្ជាក់ជំហរគោរពសេចក្តីថ្លែងការណ៍រួមកូឡាឡាំពួរលើការដោះស្រាយជម្លោះព្រំដែនជាមួយថៃ
titleEn: PM Hun Manet meets US Secretary of State via phone to confirm stance on Kuala Lumpur Statement for resolving border conflict with Thailand

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defense reported that the Thai military fired approximately 360 shells into Sok Sang and Prey Chan villages in Banteay Meanchey province between 7:00 am and 2:30 pm on December 26. The ministry described the actions as brutal and indiscriminate attacks violating international humanitarian law.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 15.20 26/12/25: 360 shells fired by Thai aggressors at 2 Cambodian villages today
titleEn: Conflict Update 15:20 26/12/25: 360 shells fired by Thai aggressors at 2 Cambodian villages today

summary: Cambodia has accused Thai forces of carrying out aerial attacks with F-16 fighter jets dropping dozens of bombs near Chouk Chey village on Friday morning. The attacks caused destruction to civilian homes and infrastructure even as both sides hold talks to ease the conflict that has killed at least 96 people since December 8.
title: Cambodia blames Thailand for ‘ruthless’ bombardment amid border talks

summary: Following three days of negotiations in Chanthaburi, the GBC secretariat teams have reached a consensus on a draft joint statement and ceasefire terms. The agreement is set to take effect on December 27. Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the Thai Defense Minister will attend the meeting today to finalize the statement under the Kuala Lumpur Agreement framework.
title: Thailand and Cambodia agree on the terms of the initial ceasefire

summary: Thailand's Defence Minister is scheduled to join border talks on Saturday, December 27, that could lead to a ceasefire agreement. Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul stated that a potential deal would align with previous agreements brokered by the US in July. Nearly one million people remain displaced by the fighting.
title: Thai Defence Minister to attend truce talks with Cambodia, PM says

summary: At 7:31 AM on December 27, 2025, Thai F-16 fighter jets reportedly dropped four bombs on Cambodian civilian areas in Kampong Svay commune, Serei Saophoan City, Banteay Meanchey province. The Ministry of Defense stated that Cambodian forces remain on high alert and vigilant to defend territorial integrity and national dignity.
title: យោធាថៃ បានប្រើយន្តហោះចម្បាំង F-16 ទម្លាក់គ្រាប់ បែកចំនួន 4គ្រាប់ ចូលទីតាំងប្រជាជនស៊ីវិលកម្ពុជា ក្នុងក្រុងសិរីសោភ័ណ នៅម៉ោង 7:31នាទីព្រឹក
titleEn: Thai military uses F-16 fighter jets to drop 4 bombs on Cambodian civilian locations in Serei Saophoan at 7:31 AM

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that as of December 26 evening, Thai military shelling and bombardment has resulted in a total of 31 deaths and 91 injuries among Cambodian civilians since December 7. The latest casualties include one death in Siem Reap and one injury in Banteay Meanchey. The report highlights severe impacts on civilian areas across multiple border provinces.
title: ក្រសួងមហាផ្ទៃ ៖ អំពើឈ្លានរបស់ថៃ លើដែនអធិបតេយ្យកម្ពុជា បណ្ដាលឱ្យពលរដ្ឋកម្ពុជាស្លាប់កើនឡើង 31នាក់ និងរបួស 91នាក់
titleEn: Ministry of Interior: Thai aggression on Cambodian sovereignty leads to 31 deaths and 91 injuries

summary: Between 7:31 AM and 8:00 AM on December 27, Thai F-16 fighter jets reportedly violated Cambodian airspace and dropped 16 bombs in Banteay Meanchey province. This incident occurred just hours before the scheduled 12:00 PM ceasefire. The report reflects the high tension and continued military activity leading up to the diplomatic agreement.
title: យោធាថៃ ប្រើ F-16 បាញ់16គ្រាប់ ចូលបន្ទាយមានជ័យ
titleEn: Thai military uses F-16s to drop 16 bombs in Banteay Meanchey

summary: Reports indicate that despite a consensus reached on ceasefire terms, the Thai military launched at least three F-16 bombing raids on December 27. At 7:00 AM, strikes targeted Anlong Veng district; at 7:30 AM and 7:31 AM, bombs were dropped on Serei Sophon city and Kampong Svay Sangkat in Banteay Meanchey province, specifically hitting civilian residential areas.
title: CONFLICT UPDATE 08.30 27/12/25: Despite apparent ceasefire agreement, Thailand launches multiple F-16 bombing raids on Cambodia this morning

summary: An editorial from the state-run news agency condemns Thailand for what it describes as systematic aggression and violation of past truces. The piece claims that while Cambodia seeks peace, Thai forces have targeted civilian infrastructure like homes, schools, and hospitals, and accuses the Thai government of creating a false narrative to mislead the international community.
title: OPINION: Thailand: How Many More Denials Will It Take to Admit It's the Aggressor?

summary: The Club of Cambodian Journalists (CCJ) distributed protective vests and helmets to 57 journalists from 36 media organizations to ensure their safety while reporting from high-risk zones along the Cambodia-Thailand border. This move comes as security risks remain elevated despite ongoing diplomatic talks.
title: Club of Cambodian Journalists distributes protective gear to border reporters

summary: To prevent misunderstandings and manage incidents on the ground promptly, both sides have agreed to create a joint border coordination unit. This unit is intended to verify that the ceasefire is being respected and to maintain direct communication between local commanders to avoid accidental escalations.
title: អង្គភាពសម្របសម្រួលព្រំដែនមួយនឹងត្រូវបង្កើតដើម្បីធានាពីអនុវត្តបទឈប់បាញ់
titleEn: A border coordination unit will be established to ensure the implementation of the ceasefire

summary: Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence Tea Seiha announced that Cambodia and Thailand have agreed on an immediate ceasefire effective from 12:00 PM on December 27, 2025. The agreement, reached during the 3rd Special Meeting of the General Border Committee (GBC) in Pailin, requires both sides to maintain current positions for at least 72 hours to ensure full implementation. ASEAN observers were present at the meeting.
title: បទឈប់បាញ់ រវាងកម្ពុជា-ថៃ ត្រូវអនុវត្តឲ្យពេញលេង
titleEn: Ceasefire between Cambodia and Thailand must be fully implemented

summary: Defense Minister Tea Seiha announced that if the ceasefire holds for 72 hours, Thailand will release 18 Cambodian soldiers detained for 151 days. The minister also noted that displaced residents are being encouraged to return home under provincial guidance. Additionally, Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn is scheduled to attend a trilateral meeting with Thailand and China in Yunnan on Dec 28-29 to discuss further stabilization.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Agree on Ceasefire at Special GBC Meeting

summary: Following the 3rd Special GBC meeting, a joint statement confirmed an immediate ceasefire starting at 12:00 PM on Dec 27. A critical component of the deal is the repatriation of 18 Cambodian soldiers held by Thailand for 151 days; their release is contingent on the ceasefire being fully maintained for 72 hours. The agreement also covers demining cooperation and efforts to combat transnational cybercrime.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Agree to Ceasefire Effective Noon Dec. 27

summary: Article 11 of the new border accord stipulates that 18 Cambodian soldiers captured during the July 2025 clashes will be returned home. This repatriation is contingent on the current ceasefire being successfully maintained for a period of 72 hours without violations.
title: 18 Cambodian soldiers, held by Thailand for over 150 days, to be released – if ceasefire holds
titleEn: 18 Cambodian soldiers held by Thailand for 150 days to be released if ceasefire holds

summary: To ensure the truce holds, both nations have agreed to use Border Coordination Units to manage ground situations and prevent miscalculations. The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) will play a role in verification. Direct communication lines remain open between Defense Ministers and Chiefs of Defense Forces.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Outlines Mechanisms for Effective Ceasefire Implementation

summary: State media confirms the ceasefire signing by Tea Seiha and Nattaphon Narkphanit. A critical provision includes the return of 18 captured Cambodian soldiers once the ceasefire is maintained for 72 hours. It also emphasizes the protection of civilians and the resumption of joint demining efforts.
title: Cambodia, Thailand Agree on Immediate Ceasefire Effective from Noon

summary: Envoys and governments from China, Japan, Australia, Germany, and the EU issued statements welcoming the December 27 ceasefire. Chinese Ambassador Wang Wenbin expressed hope that the lives of people on both sides would return to normal soon, while Germany and Australia emphasized the need for continued dialogue toward a durable peace.
title: International Community Welcomes Cambodia-Thailand Ceasefire, Urges Effective Implementation

summary: Cambodia and Thailand signed a 16-point Joint Statement at the 3rd Special General Border Committee (GBC) meeting. The agreement mandates an immediate ceasefire starting at noon on December 27, 2025. It includes provisions to halt all weapon use, stop troop movements, and refrain from spreading 'fake news' to de-escalate public sentiment.
title: BREAKING NEWS: Cambodia and Thailand agree to ‘immediate ceasefire after the time of signature of this Joint Statement with effect from 12:00 hours noon (local time) on 27 December 2025’
titleEn: BREAKING NEWS: Cambodia and Thailand agree to immediate ceasefire effective 12:00 PM Dec 27

summary: Following the 3rd Special General Border Committee (GBC) meeting, both nations signed a 16-point Joint Statement. The agreement mandates an immediate ceasefire effective noon Dec 27, a freeze on all troop movements, and a prohibition on attacks against civilians and infrastructure. It explicitly states the arrangements are without prejudice to border demarcation, which remains under the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC).
title: Cambodia–Thailand sign detailed border accord outlining ceasefire, de-escalation and verification measures

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has appealed to Cambodian citizens to remain calm and maintain their dignity. He specifically urged people to avoid any discrimination or hostile actions against the Thai embassy, Thai companies, or Thai citizens residing in Cambodia, emphasizing that the focus should remain on the peaceful diplomatic resolution.
title: កម្ពុជា-ថៃ ឯកភាពគ្នាលើបទឈប់បាញ់ ដោយអនុវត្តចាប់ពីម៉ោង12៖00ថ្ងៃត្រង់ ថ្ងៃទី27 ខែធ្នូ ឆ្នាំ2025
titleEn: Cambodia-Thailand agree on ceasefire, effective from 12:00 noon, December 27, 2025

summary: Cambodian media emphasizes the humanitarian aspects of the new agreement, highlighting the pledge to avoid using any weapons against civilians. The report also mentions that the European Union has offered satellite imagery to monitor the ceasefire, while Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim has been in contact with both PM Hun Manet and Thai leadership to facilitate the resolution.
title: កម្ពុជា-ថៃ ឯកភាពគ្នា មិនបង្កើនកម្លាំងតាមបណ្តោយព្រំដែន និងមិនប្រើកម្លាំងគ្រប់ប្រភេទ ប្រឆាំងនឹងជនស៊ីវិល
titleEn: Cambodia-Thailand agree not to increase forces along the border and not to use any kind of force against civilians

summary: Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, Spokeswoman of the Ministry of National Defence, confirmed that the frontline remained calm between 12:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. following the signing of the ceasefire at the 3rd Special GBC Meeting. She stated that Cambodian forces are committed to the agreement but remain vigilant. Government spokesperson Pen Bona urged the public to read the full Joint Statement to avoid misinformation.
title: Battlefields Along Cambodia-Thailand Border Are Calm

summary: A total of 101 people have died and over 500,000 have been displaced during the 20 days of fighting. The new ceasefire, which took effect Saturday noon, has reportedly held into Sunday with no reports of gunfire. The deal includes the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers if the peace holds for 72 hours and monitoring by an ASEAN observer team.
title: Thailand and Cambodia agree to second ceasefire

summary: Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn is attending a trilateral meeting with the Foreign Ministers of Thailand and China in Yunnan, China, on December 28-29. The meeting, hosted by Wang Yi, aims to strengthen mutual trust, reduce tensions, and restore peace to the border area following the 20-day conflict.
title: Trilateral meeting today on the current situation between Cambodia and Thailand will be held under the coordination of China

summary: Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, Spokeswoman of the Ministry of National Defence, confirmed that the frontline situation has remained calm since the ceasefire took effect at noon on December 27. Cambodian forces are following the joint statement's rules, which prohibit troop movements, patrols, and the use of all types of weapons. The ministry emphasized that the agreement is without prejudice to future border demarcation.
title: Cambodia-Thailand Border Remains Calm

summary: This report highlights the human cost of the 26-day conflict, noting that 42 schools in Banteay Meanchey remain closed. It promotes the Cambodian leadership's 'Win-Win' policy as the solution to return to normalcy. It also notes reports of Chinese nationals being injured by landmines along the border and stresses that peace must be prioritized to allow development to resume.
title: «ឈប់បាញ់ ឈប់បង្ហូរឈាម ងាកទៅរកការចរចាវិញ តើមានអ្វីប្រសើរជាងនេះ?»
titleEn: Ceasefire, stop the bloodshed, turn back to negotiations: Is there anything better?

summary: Following the ceasefire that took effect at noon on December 27, several world powers that assisted in mediating the conflict have issued messages of support and congratulations. The report frames the ceasefire as a successful outcome of the 3rd Special General Boundary Committee (GBC) meeting.
title: មហាអំណាចក្នុងពិភពលោក ស្វាគមន៍បទឈប់បាញ់កម្ពុជា-ថៃ
titleEn: World powers welcome Cambodia-Thailand ceasefire

summary: Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Kunming. He expressed deep gratitude for China's active and constructive role in supporting the ceasefire and pushing for a diplomatic resolution based on mutual respect and long-term peace.
title: ប្រមុខការទូតកម្ពុជា៖ កិច្ចគាំទ្រជាបន្តបន្ទាប់របស់មិត្តចិន ដើរតួនាទីយ៉ាងសំខាន់ ក្នុងការគាំទ្រដល់ការអនុវត្តបទឈប់បាញ់ពេញលេញ
titleEn: Cambodian Foreign Minister: China's Support Plays Crucial Role in Supporting Full Ceasefire Implementation

summary: Vong Soth, Second Vice President of the National Assembly, distributed aid including 3,500kg of rice, milk, blankets, and clothing to displaced families in Phnom Srok District. The report claims over half a million Cambodian civilians were forced to flee since armed conflict reignited on December 7, 2025. Local officials vowed transparent distribution to those affected by the war.
title: អនុប្រធានទី2នៃរដ្ឋសភា ផ្តល់អំណោយសម្ភារ គ្រឿងឧបភោគ និងបរិភោគ ជួយសម្រាលបន្ទុកពលរដ្ឋភៀសសឹក នៅស្រុកភ្នំស្រុក ខេត្តបន្ទាយមានជ័យ
titleEn: Second Vice President of the National Assembly provides aid to war-displaced citizens in Banteay Meanchey

summary: General Maly Socheata, spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense, stated that following the immediate ceasefire agreement signed on December 27, the situation along the border has been quiet with no unusual incidents. However, she emphasized that Cambodian troops continue to monitor the situation strictly and remain on standby.
title: លោកស្រី ម៉ាលី សុជាតា ៖ ស្ថានភាពព្រំដែនស្ងប់ស្ងាត់ តែកម្លាំងកម្ពុជាតាមដានជាប់ជានិច្ច
titleEn: Ms. Maly Socheata: Border situation is quiet, but Cambodian forces are monitoring constantly

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Information issued a clarification regarding rumors that the ceasefire signed on December 27 is only valid for 72 hours. The Ministry stated this is a misconception, affirming that the ceasefire is intended for 'long-term peace.' The 72-hour period mentioned in the accord specifically relates to an observation window after which 18 detained Cambodian soldiers will be released by Thailand.
title: Ministry issues statement, following misunderstanding of Ceasefire duration

summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued a statement welcoming the Dec 27 ceasefire. The US urged both nations to immediately honor the commitment and fully implement the terms of the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accords to ensure stability.
title: US Welcomes Cambodia–Thailand Ceasefire, Urges Full Implementation of Peace Accords

summary: Despite the Dec 27 ceasefire, many displaced civilians in Cambodia's Banteay Meanchey and Thailand's Sisaket provinces remain in shelters, citing a lack of trust in the opposing military. While some Thai farmers plan to return to their cattle, many Cambodians fear fighting could resume at any time.
title: Border ceasefire brings hope but evacuees in Thailand and Cambodia remain wary

summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced on his social media platform Truth Social that the fighting between Thailand and Cambodia has officially ended. He stated that the two nations will return to peace in accordance with the original treaty recently agreed upon.
title: Trump declares Thailand-Cambodia conflict over

source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China
summary: Foreign Ministers of China, Cambodia, and Thailand met in Yunnan on Dec 28-29. They agreed to consolidate the ceasefire, ensure the full implementation of the Dec 27 Joint Statement, and cooperate on humanitarian de-mining. China pledged to provide support for the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT).
title: Press Release of China-Cambodia-Thailand Fuxian Meeting

summary: A day after the ceasefire began, Cambodian refugees have started returning to border villages. However, government officials warn that many areas remain dangerous due to unexploded ordnance and landmines. Returning families face severe economic hardship and the task of rebuilding homes destroyed during the 20 days of fighting.
title: Refugees begin trickling back to their villages, but not everyone can go home as some border areas remain unsafe

summary: Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn emphasized the geographical reality that both nations must live together peacefully. Speaking after trilateral talks in China, he stated that the priority is to return border communities to their 'pre-conflict' status, where people traded and lived together without fear. He noted that peace is a shared desire for both Khmer and Thai border residents.
title: “We Are Permanent Neighbours, We Cannot Move Our Borders” - Prak Sokhonn Calls for Peace Between Cambodia and Thailand

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet issued a message clarifying that the Dec 27 ceasefire is not a surrender or a trade-off of territorial integrity. He emphasized that the decision was made to prioritize the lives of over 500,000 displaced civilians and soldiers' families. He noted that while Cambodia is a small country, it maintains the right to self-defense, but currently prioritizes the return of children to schools and families to their homes. He stated that 32 civilians have died and 93 were injured in the conflict so far.
title: សម្តេច ហ៊ុន ម៉ាណែត៖ រើសអនុវត្តបទឈប់បាញ់មិនមែនកម្ពុជាចាញ់ ឬ សុខចិត្តយកបូរណភាពទឹកដី ទៅដូរយកសន្តិភាពឡើយ
titleEn: PM Hun Manet: Choosing Ceasefire Doesn't Mean Cambodia Loses or Trades Sovereignty for Peace

summary: The Minister of Information, Neth Pheaktra, has officially denied rumors circulating on social media claiming that Thai military forces arrested 10 additional Cambodian soldiers at the Ta Thav border gate. He labeled these reports as 'fake news' designed to cause public confusion and damage the stability of the current border management.
title: ការផ្សព្វផ្សាយថា ថៃចាប់ទ័ពកម្ពុជា 10នាក់ទៀត ជារឿងមិនពិត
titleEn: Reports that Thailand arrested 10 more Cambodian soldiers are untrue

summary: The Cambodia-Thailand-China meeting in Yunnan concluded with a five-point consensus: consolidating the ceasefire, resuming normal exchanges, rebuilding political trust, improving bilateral ties, and safeguarding regional stability. China pledged immediate humanitarian aid for displaced persons and support for demining efforts through a Joint Coordinating Task Force.
title: Trilateral Meeting Achieves Five Key Outcomes to Restore Cambodia-Thailand Relations

summary: Defense Ministry spokesperson Mali Socheata stated during a press conference that the situation along the border in the 4th and 5th Military Regions has been quiet following the ceasefire. However, Cambodian forces remain on high alert and are strictly monitoring the situation to protect sovereignty and territorial integrity.
title: រហូតមកដល់ថ្ងៃទី2 នៃបទឈប់បាញ់ ស្ថានភាពព្រំដែន ស្ងប់ស្ងាត់
titleEn: Border Situation Remains Calm on the Second Day of Ceasefire

summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn announced on December 29 that, pending any last-minute changes, 18 Cambodian soldiers arrested by Thailand in June 2025 are scheduled for release at 12:00 PM on December 30. The release is a direct result of the ceasefire agreement reached on December 27 and is being coordinated by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
title: DPM: If nothing changes, at 12 noon tomorrow, Cambodia will welcome back 18 soldiers held captive for 150 days by Thailand.

summary: Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn announced following a trilateral meeting with China and Thailand in Yunnan that 18 Cambodian soldiers held for 151 days are scheduled for release at 12:00 PM on December 30. This marks the end of the required 72-hour period during which the ceasefire must be fully maintained.
title: 18 Cambodian Soldiers Expected to Be Released on December 30

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Defence reported that as of December 29, the situation in Military Regions 4 and 5 (bordering Thailand) remains calm following the December 27 ceasefire. However, the ministry emphasized that armed forces remain in place and are maintaining high vigilance to defend national sovereignty.
title: Defence Ministry Confirms Stability along Cambodia–Thailand Border, Cambodian Armed Forces Maintain Vigilance

summary: Spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defence, Lt. Gen. Mali Socheata, denied Thai claims that over 250 drones from Cambodia violated Thai airspace on December 29. She stated that Cambodia is strictly adhering to the GBC joint statement and the ceasefire, and has issued strict bans on any drone flights in border provinces.
title: កម្ពុជា ពុំបានបង្ហោះយានគ្មានមនុស្សបើកជាង 250គ្រឿង ចូលរំលោភដែនអធិបតេយ្យរបស់ថៃទេ
titleEn: Cambodia did not launch more than 250 UAVs to violate Thailand's sovereignty

summary: Phnom Penh has proposed an urgent special meeting with Thailand to resume the work of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC). The goal is to address stalled border survey and demarcation work following the recent ceasefire agreement. This move is seen as an effort to resolve underlying territorial disputes that triggered the recent armed conflict.
title: Cambodia seeks meeting with Thailand to resume demarcation

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized in a national message that the ceasefire is not a surrender or cession of territory. He stated that the decision was made to protect the lives of civilians, noting that 32 civilians have been killed and 93 injured in the conflict so far. He highlighted that the international boundary remains governed by existing treaties and the ceasefire allows half a million displaced people to return home.
title: Cambodia agreed to ceasefire to protect its people from the pain of conflict, says Prime Minister

summary: The Ministry of National Defence of Cambodia has categorically rejected Thailand's claim that over 250 drones flew from Cambodia into Thai airspace on December 29. Spokeswoman Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata called the allegations unfounded and reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to the December 27 ceasefire. She noted that strict instructions have been issued to provincial authorities to prohibit all drone launches.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Claim of Drone Incursions, Reaffirms Commitment to Ceasefire

summary: Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, spokeswoman for the Ministry of National Defence, stated on December 30 that the 72-hour deadline for full ceasefire implementation has been reached. She reported that the situation along the Cambodia-Thailand border remains calm and stable. This follows the agreement reached during the GBC meeting on December 27.
title: គ្រប់3ថ្ងៃ នៃការអនុវត្ត បទឈប់បាញ់ពេញលេញ សភាពការណ៍ នៅព្រំដែន មានលក្ខណៈស្ងប់ស្ងាត់ល្អ
titleEn: After 3 days of full ceasefire implementation, the border situation remains calm

summary: Following weeks of intense fighting that killed over 100 people and displaced 440,000 Cambodians, Caritas Cambodia has launched an emergency appeal to support 5,000 families in 20 priority camps. The aid includes food, shelter kits, solar lights, and psychosocial support for children traumatized by artillery fire and air strikes. Over 315,000 people are currently sheltering in 200 government evacuation sites facing overcrowding and poor sanitation.
title: Caritas Cambodia steps up aid for displaced families along the Thailand–Cambodia border

summary: Foreign ministers from China, Cambodia, and Thailand met on December 29 to discuss the border crisis. The priority is to ensure the ceasefire remains effective. They agreed to support the Joint Border Committee (JBC) to demarcate the border according to international law and the UN Charter. China is ready to help with humanitarian demining through the Joint Coordination Task Force (JCTF) and support ASEAN Observers (AOT).
title: ចិន កម្ពុជា ថៃ គាំទ្រដល់គណៈកម្មការចម្រុះខ័ណ្ឌសីមាព្រំដែន និងច្បាប់ UN ដើម្បីបញ្ចប់វិវិវាទកម្ពុជា-ថៃ
titleEn: China, Cambodia, Thailand support Joint Border Committee and UN Law to end Cambodia-Thailand dispute

summary: During a trilateral meeting in Yunnan, China, Deputy PM Prak Sokhonn emphasized that Cambodia and Thailand are permanent neighbors and must ensure peace. He thanked China for its role in facilitating the December 27 ceasefire. China announced 20 million RMB in humanitarian aid for Cambodian IDPs. Sokhonn also held bilateral talks with Thai FM Sihasak Phuangketkeow to reaffirm commitment to the ceasefire and the General Border Committee (GBC) joint statement.
title: DPM Prak Sokhonn: Cambodia and Thailand Share Responsibility to Ensure Regional Peace and Stability

summary: As of 5:10 PM on December 30, the 72-hour ceasefire deadline for the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers has passed without their return. Families and provincial governors, including Pailin Governor Ban Sreymom, reported having no information on the release. The situation is complicated by Thai allegations of 250 Cambodian drone incursions and a landmine incident, which Cambodia's Ministry of National Defense has refuted. Over 590,000 Cambodians remain in displacement shelters.
title: First 72-hours of Ceasefire Expires As Families Await Release of 18 Captured Soldiers

summary: Experts and social observers warn that while physical fighting has stopped, a 'Digitalization War' continues online. They claim Thailand is using fake news and AI-generated content to poison the information environment and cause confusion among Cambodians. The Ministry of Information urged citizens to only follow official government sources to avoid falling into psychological traps.
title: សង្គ្រាមនៅលើសមរភូមិស្ងប់ស្ងាត់ហើយ នៅឡើយតែសង្គ្រាមព័ត៌មាន តើពលរដ្ឋគួរធ្វើដូចម្តេច ដើម្បីកុំឱ្យចាញ់សង្គ្រាមចិត្តសាស្ត្រ?
titleEn: War on the battlefield is quiet, but information war remains; what should citizens do to avoid losing the psychological war?

summary: The 18 Cambodian soldiers captured in July 2025 were released at the Prum-Ban Pak Kard border crossing. They were transported to Phnom Penh where thousands of citizens lined the streets to welcome them. The article frames their detention as 'illegal' and highlights their meeting with Prime Minister Hun Manet. International observers like the ICRC and EU welcomed the move as a step toward rebuilding trust.
title: 18 soldiers illegally detained in Thailand for five months come home to a hero's welcome

summary: A highly critical analysis accusing the Thai military of transforming a border row into an 'undeclared war.' The article claims the conflict displaced over 640,000 Cambodians and damaged UNESCO-listed sites like Preah Vihear. Experts quoted in the piece describe Thailand's actions as reflecting 'expansionist ambitions' and a refusal to respect historical treaties (1904/1907) and ICJ rulings.
title: How a border dispute turned into a full-scale invasion of Cambodia

summary: The National Bank of Cambodia (NBC) has issued an urgent announcement to all banking and financial institutions to prioritize debt relief and credit restructuring for soldiers and veterans. This comes after a significant surge in applications for financial assistance from military personnel following the border conflict. The central bank aim to prevent logistical bottlenecks and ensure support for those who served on the frontlines.
title: National Bank Urges Debt Relief Priority for Frontline Soldiers

summary: Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that conditions are not yet suitable for a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting proposed by Cambodia for January in Siem Reap. Thailand cited its caretaker government status and the extensive presence of landmines as obstacles to survey and demarcation work. Cambodia had previously sent a diplomatic note to initiate these talks.
title: Conditions not yet met for border meeting with Cambodia: Thai FM spokesperson

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona reaffirmed that Cambodia strictly adheres to the December 27 Joint Statement and will not recognize any border adjustments made through military force. He emphasized that the current deployment of troops does not affect official boundary demarcation.
title: អ្នកនាំពាក្យរាជរដ្ឋាភិបាលបញ្ជាក់ឡើងវិញថា កម្ពុជាមិនទទួលស្គាល់ការកែប្រែព្រំដែន ដោយការប្រើកម្លាំងនោះទេ
titleEn: Government Spokesperson Reaffirms: Cambodia will not recognize boundary changes by force

summary: Senate President Hun Sen expressed his deep sympathy for the 18 soldiers who returned after 155 days of separation from their families. He compared their experience to his own struggles and highlighted the government's commitment to 'leaving no soldier behind.' The government has also established a task force to restore infrastructure and livelihoods damaged during the conflict.
title: សម្តេចតេជោ យល់ទុក្ខលំបាករបស់វីរយុទ្ធជនកម្ពុជា18រូបបែកបាក់ពីគ្រួសារ
titleEn: Samdech Techo understands the hardships of the 18 Cambodian heroic soldiers separated from their families

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MFAIC) issued a statement welcoming the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers who had been held for 155 days. The soldiers were repatriated via the Prum International Point of Entry in Pailin province on December 31. The ministry stated that this move will contribute to building mutual trust and creating an environment for normalizing relations. The process was observed by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
title: Release of 18 Cambodian Soldiers Seen as Step Toward Restoring Peace and Trust

summary: King Norodom Sihamoni and the Queen Mother received the 18 recently released Cambodian soldiers at the Royal Palace. The soldiers, who were held by Thai authorities since fighting began in July 2025, were presented with royal gifts. This high-profile reception followed earlier meetings with Prime Minister Hun Manet and Senate President Hun Sen, underscoring the soldiers' status as national heroes in Cambodia.
title: King Sihamoni, Queen Mother Grant Royal Audience to Freed Cambodian Soldiers
